findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.citation_text:
3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT (RTE) FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

A food handler was observed to handled cooked RTE foods as they were moving them to cold holding/cooling. Education was conducted with the PIC and should be trickled down to staff moving forward. Tongs or gloves are needed to handle RTE foods that do not have another kill step prior to service. Ensure that all RTE foods are handled safely at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above.

Cooked steak was observed in a pan at 120F internal temperatures. The pan is attempting a double boiler style of hot holding but the edges of the pans do not meet. This is allowing the hot air and steam to escape as apposed to being trapped and transferring the heat to the TCS foods. The procedures in place are not allowing for effective hot holding of the foods. Per the PIC the steak was prepared at noon and placed in the hot holding at that time. This puts the four hour limit for foods being out of temperature at 4 pm that afternoon. The PIC was instructed to discard the foods at that time, and they did. A new situation for the hot holding of these foods will need to be put in place moving forward.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. 

A mop was observed stored with the head pooled up in the bottom of the mop sink. The PIC was shown and moved the mop so that it would drip/air dry effectively. Ensure that the mops are stored so that they effectively dry each time in the facility.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

At the beginning of this inspection there was not a certified food protection manager (CFPM) available at this facility. The PIC was consulted and called the owner during the inspection. They arrived to correct the immediate violation. They were instructed to ensure that there are sufficient CFPMs on staff to cover all shifts.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. 

An employee was observed to dump a sani bucket into a hand sink during the inspection. Education was conducted to correct. Ensure that hand sinks are only used for hand washing and no other purpose int he facility.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
(REPEAT x2) 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

The sani buckets in the front of the kitchen as well as the bar area were observed low at the beginning of the inspection. The PIC was shown and remade the buckets during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all sanitizers are at effective levels at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section.

1) A container of salsa in the walk-in cooler was observed with an incorrect date. The cook stated that the sticker would not come off when washed. 2) A container of pico was observed without a date marking in the walk in cooler. Both locations were discussed with the PIC and corrected during this inspection. Ensure that date marking is correctly managed by all employees in the facility at all times.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.citation_text:
3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

A bag of onion were observed stored on the floor in the kitchen. The cook was shown and the onions moved to correct. Ensure that all foods are stored at least 6 inches above the floor to prevent possible pest concerns and contamination from the floor.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.citation_text:
5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

The sink in the bar area is leaking from both the faucet connection as well as the drain pipe. The PIC is instructed to repair prior to the next routine inspection. Ensure that all plumbing fixtures in the facility are maintained in good repair at all times.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.citation_text:
6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

An employee’s can of sprite was observed in the standing cooler next to open salsas ready for service. The PIC was consulted and instructed to store employee foods separate from foods intended for consumers moving forward. Store employee belongings in such a way so that there is not a concern for contamination of consumer foods.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

1) The dish machine was registering low on the inspector’s and facility’s test strips at the beginning of the inspection. The jug of concentrate had appeared to have off gassed. A new jug was attached to the machine and it was brought up to effective levels to correct. 2) (REPEAT) The sani buckets in the front of the kitchen as well as the bar area were observed low at the beginning of the inspection. These are the other two buckets in the facility from the one noted on the previous routine inspection and are a repeated situation. The PIC was shown and remade the buckets during this inspection to correct.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The nozzle of the Cherry Pepsi fountain drink was observed heavily soiled during the inspection. The PIC was shown and cleaned/sanitized the nozzle during the inspection to correct. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are maintained clean at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.citation_text:
6-303.11(A) Intensity. The light intensity shall be: (A) At least 108 lux (10 foot candles) at a distance of 75 cm (30 inches) above the floor, in walk-in refrigeration units and dry FOOD storage areas and in other areas and rooms during periods of cleaning;

The light in the walk in freezer would not turn on during the inspection. The inspector returned to this location at the end of the inspection as the PIC indicated that it would take a short while for the bulbs to warm up. The room was still dark at the later observation point even thought the light was left on. The inspector also turned the light off and back on and waited a few minutes to no avail. The PIC is instructed to exchange the bulbs (most likely fix) or contact an electrician if new bulbs do not fix the issue prior to the next routine inspection. The freezer must have effective lighting to ensure food and employee safety. Ensure effective lighting at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

At the time of this inspection there is not a certified food protection manager (CFPM) available at this facility. The PIC was consulted and instructed to ensure that there are sufficient CFPMs on staff to cover all shifts. A CFPM arrived during this inspection to correct the immediate concern. Hand outs were given for local CFPM courses as well as the CFPM courses provided by SCDPH in the coming year.

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.citation_text:
3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

The handle of the scoop used for dispensing ice in the server area is observed in contact with the ice. The PIC removed the scoop prior to discussion. Violation considered corrected at this time. Ensure that bare hand contact is prevented at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The blade of the can open is observed soiled with dried on debris. The PIC was shown and instructed to maintain clean moving forward. The item was moved to dish for cleaning during this inspection to correct.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

The sani bucket in the kitchen is observed to not produce a color change on the inspector’s test strips. The cook was in the process of changing the buckets as the inspector came from the bar area. The violation is considered CORRECTED at this time but. No color change at all on the test strips indicates that the solution had not been effective for a while prior to observation. Ensure sanitizers are changed often enough to be maintained at effective concentration.

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.citation_text:
3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

The handle of the scoop used for dispensing ice is observed in contact with the ice. The PIC removed the scoop prior to discussion. Violation considered corrected at this time. Ensure that bare hand contact is prevented at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. 

On arrival the inspector observed a pitcher of soaking drink jug lids in the hand sink in the server area. They removed the pitcher to allow for hand washing to correct the violation. Ensure that hand sinks are maintained readily accessible for hand washing as well as only used for hand washing at all times.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 Food Contact with Equipment and Utensils. FOOD shall only contact surfaces of: (A) EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS that are cleaned as specified under Part 4-6 of this Code and SANITIZED as specified under Part 4-7 of this Code; (B) Single-service and single-use articles; or (C) LINENS, such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3-304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code. 

A drink can is observed submerged in the ice in the ice machine. The PIC was shown and the can removed to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that ready to eat (RTE) foods (ice) only contact cleaned and sanitized surfaces prior to consumption moving forward.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. 

There is a container of spoiled vegetables in the walk in used for dry storage. Numerous flies are observed in, on and around this container. The PIC was shown and discarded the containers which removed a large section of these flies immediately. The inspector will check in a couple weeks to ensure that none of these pests remain.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

At the time of this inspection there is not a certified food protection manager (CFPM) available at this facility. The PIC was consulted and instructed to ensure that there are sufficient CFPMs on staff to cover all shifts.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11(A) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (A) Equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be cleaned: (5) At any time during the operation when contamination may have occurred.

1) Multiple sets of tongs in the storage room are observed with remaining food debris; 2) Tubs in the storage room are observed with remaining food debris; 3) Multiple knives in the knife block are observed with remaining food debris on them. All three situations were shown to the PIC and moved back to dish for re-cleaning. This situation has been noted multiple times in the past. Management should educate staff and ensure that all food contact surfaces are being completely cleaned prior to storage. Inspector will spot check moving forward to ensure that complaince is ongoing for this situation.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.citation_text:
6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors. 

The back door to the facility does not seal completely during this inspection. The PIC was shown and instructed to repair the door/seal prior to the next routine inspection. Ensure that all outer openings are protected from pest entry at all times.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.citation_text:
3-305.14 Food Preparation. During preparation, unPACKAGED FOOD shall be protected from environmental sources of contamination. 

Peppers and tomato sauce are observed remaining in their cans after opening and during storage. No covering is being provided beyond the open can top. The PIC was shown the jalapeño peppers in the walk in cooler and instructed to store all foods in sealable containers after opening.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

A pair of cloths next to the hand sink in the server area are observed on the counter and not in a sanitizer solution. The PIC was shown and instructed to maintain the rags used for wiping counters and other food contact surfaces in solution of effective concentration between uses at all times. The rags were moved to a bucket to correct.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

Multiple shelves throughout the facility are observed with chipping paint and rust. The PIC was shown an example and instructed to clean and re-seal the shelving units throughout the facility. Provide a smooth and easily cleanable surface for any potential food related surfaces.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. 

There is not currently a PIC with a current allergen certification training available during this inspection. The PIC was consulted and instructed to ensure that there is always a CFPM on site with allergen training. A copy of the certificate should be maintained at the facility at all times.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. 

A quarter pan of shrimp was observed in the hand sink next to the prep area. The PIC was shown and the shrimp moved to a cooler to correct. Ensure that the hand sinks are maintained accessible at all times. This is the second inspection where a hand sink had items in it preventing its intended use (hand washing). Ensure that all hand sink are maintained accessible at all times.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

1) The nozzles of the soda fountain drink machine are observed soiled. Per the PIC they should be being cleaned nightly. This does not appear to be the case at this time. The nozzles were removed and cleaned/sanitized during this inspection to correct the immediate violation. Ensure staff is trained and consistent in their cleaning practices. 2) The deflector shield of the ice machine has slime/mold growth beginning. The location was shown to and discussed with the PIC. They cleaned/sanitized it during this inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that the food contact surfaces are maintained clean and sanitized at all times.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-602.11: (A) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned before each use, each time there is a change in work, between uses of raw FOODS to RTE FOODS, before using FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE, and when contamination has occurred. (C) Cleaned at least every 4 hours. 

1) Multiple sets of tongs in the storage room are observed with remaining food debris. 2) Multiple tubs in the storage room are observed with remaining food debris on them. 3) Multiple knives in the knife blocks are observed with remaining food debris on them. All three situations were shown to and discussed with the PIC during this inspection. The items were all moved to dish for re-cleaning to correct the immediate violation. This situation has come up multiple times in the past inspections and should be monitored by management to ensure that the dish washers are cleaning all food contact surfaces completely at all times.

findings.title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure
findings.comment:
5-103.11: (B) Hot water generation and distribution systems shall be sufficient to meet the peak hot water demands. 

The hand sink in the front of the kitchen does not currently have hot water. Ensure that the sink is repaired. Any hand washing sink is required to provide hot water when in use.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment:
5-205.15: A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW; P and (B) Maintained in good repair. 

1) The three part sink in the kitchen has a leaking faucet currently being managed with a glove wrapped around the leaking joint. 2) The bar three part sink has a leaking joint currently being managed by a hand towel. The two locations were discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to repair prior to the follow up. The follow up is being scheduled as a Pf to overlap with the existing follow up on 9/16/24.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-602.11: (A) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned before each use, each time there is a change in work, between uses of raw FOODS to RTE FOODS, before using FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE, and when contamination has occurred. (C) Cleaned at least every 4 hours. 

Knives in the storage rack next to the kitchen entryway are observed to still be soiled. One is observed soiled and still wet from cleaning. Food contact surfaces should be COMPLETELY cleaned prior to storage/use. This prevent pathogenic development on the food contact surface, but also on the inside of the storage equipment which can then contaminate other utensils stored in the equipment. The knives were moved to dish for re-cleaning.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
3-305.14: During preparation, unPACKAGED FOOD shall be protected from environmental sources of contamination. 

Multiple items in the walk in freezer are on trays and without covers. The PIC was shown and instructed to maintain all foods covered when not in use. An employee was instructed to cover these items and was observed entering with Suran Wrap to correct the violation.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
3-305.14: During preparation, unPACKAGED FOOD shall be protected from environmental sources of contamination. 

Cheese is observed being shredded for Queso during this inspection. A plastic bag (Wal-Mart style) is observed being used to direct the cheese out of the shredding machine and into the waiting jug. These bags are not considered clean/safe food contact surfaces and this practice should cease. Education was conducted and the bag removed to correct. Another method will need to be developed if aiming the equipment remains a concern.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. 

The knife rack noted in line item #16 has food debris under it where the bottom is open, indicating that it is soiled inside and in need of cleaning. The rack was moved to dish and disassembled for detail cleaning. Maintain The equipment clean by preventative methods as well as regular cleaning. The space under was cleaned at this time as well.
